name: Defacement
description: Adversaries may modify visual content available internally or externally to an enterprise network, thus affecting the integrity of the original content. Reasons for [Defacement](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1491) include delivering messaging, intimidation, or claiming (possibly false) credit for an intrusion. Disturbing or offensive images may be used as a part of [Defacement](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1491) in order to cause user discomfort, or to pressure compliance with accompanying messages.

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.name: Cloud Storage Access
telemetry.description: Access to stored cloud data, including reads and provider-supported access outcomes.
telemetry.collection_focus: Explicitly select relevant object-read data events; keep principal, key, request ID and result without object contents.

providers.name: AWS CloudTrail for S3
providers.scope: Bucket control-plane events and explicitly selected object data events.

providers.name: Google Cloud Audit Logs
providers.scope: Cloud Storage access requires the relevant audit category and permissions.

providers.name: Azure storage resource logs
providers.scope: Use resource-specific data-plane diagnostics; Activity Log alone does not describe blob reads.

configuration: Choose only the lab buckets/containers and prefixes. Enable read/write data-event collection when object access is needed; management events alone are insufficient.
Keep administrative changes separately from object reads/writes. Set a cost budget and retention limit before enabling high-volume data logging.
Preserve object version/key, requesting identity, action, source address, result and request ID. Verify the collector actually receives one benign read and one benign write.

configuration_example.label: CloudTrail advanced event selector · example S3 prefix
configuration_example.note: Replace the placeholder with an owned lab bucket/prefix. Review costs and merge with required selectors; applying selectors can replace an existing selection. This does not enable management-event retention or object-write coverage.

telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Storage metadata, listing, object access and bucket administration are different operations. Do not equate a successful request with proven exfiltration or complete content visibility.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal and bucket/container: unusual object-read counts, transferred volume, new access pairs and bulk permission/deletion activity. Model backups, migrations and lifecycle policies separately.

telemetry.name: File Creation
telemetry.description: Creation or overwrite of a file at an observed path.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon FileCreate (11) to the lab directory; retain the process and file path. Differentiate creation/overwrite if the sensor can.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Content
telemetry.description: Packet or decoded application-protocol content visible at a network sensor.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope approved packet capture/protocol content collection to the lab flow; retain capture provenance and truncation indicators.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon ProcessCreate (1); preserve ProcessGuid and parent identifiers. Security 4688 is an alternative with separate audit/command-line settings.

strategies.name: Defacement via File and Web Content Modification Across Platforms

analytics.name: Analytic 0662
analytics.guidance: Adversary modifies website or application-hosted content via unauthorized file changes or script injections, often by exploiting web servers or CMS access.

tuning.description: Environment-specific naming of defacement-prone files like 'index.html', 'main.css', 'app.js'.
Detection based on rapid sequence of file writes and script injections within short time intervals.

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Application
log_sources.channel: Unexpected web application errors or CMS logs showing modification to index.html, default.aspx, or other public-facing files

analytics.name: Analytic 0663
analytics.guidance: Adversary gains shell access or uploads a malicious script to deface hosted web content in Nginx, Apache, or other services.

tuning.description: Regex for CMS-specific upload directories subject to defacement (e.g., wp-content/uploads).
Types of files to monitor for defacement (e.g., .html, .php, .jsp).

log_sources.name: apache:access_log
log_sources.channel: Unusual HTTP POST or PUT requests to paths such as '/uploads/', '/admin/', or CMS plugin folders

log_sources.name: linux:syslog
log_sources.channel: Unauthorized sudo or shell access, especially leading to file changes in /var/www or /srv/http

analytics.name: Analytic 0664
analytics.guidance: Adversary modifies internal or external site content through manipulated application bundles, hosted content, or web server configs.

tuning.description: Web root folders will vary depending on how services are configured on macOS (e.g., /Library/WebServer/Documents).

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Execution of unexpected terminal or web scripts modifying /Library/WebServer/Documents

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: File creation or overwrite in common web-hosting folders

analytics.name: Analytic 0665
analytics.guidance: Adversary defaces internal VM-hosted portals or web UIs by modifying static content on datastore-mounted paths.

tuning.description: Each environment’s VMFS/volume mounts will vary in name and path.

log_sources.name: esxi:vmkernel
log_sources.channel: Unauthorized file modifications within datastore volumes via shell access or vCLI

analytics.name: Analytic 0666
analytics.guidance: Adversary uses compromised instance credentials or web application access to deface content hosted in S3 buckets, Azure Blob Storage, or GCP Buckets.

tuning.description: Patterns of S3 or GCP buckets used for static website hosting may vary by organization.
Some uploads may appear benign unless enriched with user/role metadata.

mitigations.name: Data Backup
mitigations.description: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that can be used to restore organizational data.(Citation: Ready.gov IT DRP) Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery.

references.description: Ready.gov. (n.d.). IT Disaster Recovery Plan. Retrieved March 15, 2019.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
